title: Dose Control and Pulse-Counting Imaging for SEM
content: In scanning electron microscopes (SEMs), primary electron dose is a key parameter to get a better S/N ratio image and reduce radiation damage to samples. A simple way to control the dose is to vary the scan speed by changing the dwell time in each pixel. Faster scan speed is generally used for adjusting focus and astigmatism because it is responsive. However, there are some drawbacks to fast scanning. The smaller number of electrons lowers the S/N ratio. Faster scans can also produce streaking artifacts due to the slow response time of detectors. On the other hand, a slower scan speed produces a high S/N ratio in an SEM image but may make damage issues much worse due to the high dose in each pixel. One solution is to superpose the signals from multiple fast scans to achieve a high S/N ratio with minimal charging effects. The dose can also be adjusted in each pixel with a beam blanking technique [1], providing both detailed dose control and lithography.
